reference: CMS-DP-2023/081 motivates the J/psi parking-data method; the analysis payload is restricted to the requested 5--10 GeV range

campaign_inputs.run2024i_policy: Use one MINIv6NANOv15 production per primary dataset and exclude duplicated MINIv6NANOv15_v2 processing.
campaign_inputs.mc_campaign_note: SPS-JpsiJpsiToMuMuEE supplies a muon-trigger side and a J/psi-to-electron probe side in one event.

binning_policy: Use 5--7 and 7--10 GeV bins. The already-produced 10--15 GeV source histogram is excluded exactly before fitting and is not part of the result or payload. The 1.44--2.5 histogram interval contains only abs(eta)>1.566 probes because the ECAL transition is removed before filling.
eta_policy: Barrel bins are 0--0.8 and 0.8--1.44; the combined endcap measurement is 1.566--2.5. The 1.44--1.566 ECAL transition is excluded.
target_selection: cutBased >= 1; miniPFRelIso_all is not an additional probe pass/fail requirement
denominator: reconstructed GSF electron with 5 < pT < 10 GeV passing the ECAL fiducial region, conversion veto, and lostHits <= 1, without a cutBased or mini-isolation requirement
tag: tight electron with pT > 5 GeV and miniPFRelIso_all < 0.1; no electron trigger-object match is applied
trigger_object_bit_source: not applicable: the reference trigger is an external displaced-muon parking trigger and no electron is trigger matched
reference_trigger_strategy: The ParkingSingleMuon displaced-muon path records the event independently of the J/psi-to-electron pair. Electron tag and probe objects have no HLT matching requirement.
adoption_gates: the parking reference path is present and fired in adopted data; it is not applied to MC
no electron trigger-object matching or electron HLT requirement enters tag or probe selection
probe pass/fail audit proves mini-isolation is absent as an additional numerator requirement
the 5--7 and 7--10 GeV bins have statistically usable passing and failing J/psi peaks
simultaneous pass/fail fit convergence in every adopted bin
bin-by-bin scale-factor stability under signal, background, pass/fail-shape, fit-window, binning, and pileup variations
